text:
ben: Deploybot says canary error spike in us-west-1, auto-rollback started. Anyone on it?
deploybot: [AUTOMATED] 2025-01-14 11:12:01 UTC: CANARY_5XX_RATE > THRESHOLD (5xx=2.8%, th=1.0%). Auto-rollback initiated: candidate v4.2.0 -> stable v4.1.5. Rolling canary 12% -> 0% over 3m.
nora: I'm seeing repeated kvcache timeouts and a new shader compile log around the spike. Could be the new jit compile flag.
sre_lead: pulling node logs. If it's compile-related we can either let rollback finish (fast) or pause and flip flag then re-run canary (smaller blast).
ben: Quick check: do pinned dedicated pools get affected?
rachael: Dedicated pools are pinned; auto-rollback affects hosted canary only.
ora: I vote pause + hotfix to avoid churn.
sre_lead: Commands if we pause: `deploybot pause --tag v4.2.0 --deployment canary` and `rollback-runner abort --thread 1745554321`.
ben: Pausing now and starting a cherrypick to revert jit flag.
deploybot: [SYSTEM] Auto-rollback suppression enabled for tag v4.2.0 (expires 50m).
ops_bot: Note: if rollback had completed we'd need release_notes_unwind. Since we paused and hotfixed, mark incident=mitigated_hotfix.
rachael: Hotfix PR #4620 opened (revert: enable-jit-optim). Rolling to 1 canary node.
sre_lead: After patch: kvcache timeouts stopped, 5xx dropped to 0.4% in 3m.
ben: Keep canary pinned 25m for telemetry then finish rollout. Assign postmortem: nora (root cause), rachael (release notes), ben (rollout ops).
deploybot: [SYSTEM] Auto-rollback suppression expired for tag v4.2.0; standard rollout resumed.
ben: End of thread: rollout completed with hotfix, no dedicated impact. :white_check_mark:
